name: "Sable"
role: Informant, Port Authority Lost Property Office

nodes.line: Don't stand still. Standing still is how the billboards read you. Walk. Talk while you walk.

options.label: Ask about the grid
options.response: Eight million stories and every single one has a lens on it. The trick isn't hiding. It's being boring at scale.

options.label: Ask about a routing cover sheet
options.response: Everything exists in this city if you know where to look. One cover sheet, slightly pre-owned. The previous owner was a form. The form is fine.

options.label: Mention the Form 27-B you are definitely not filling in
options.response: 27-B? Cute. In this city forms breed in filing cabinets. Yours already has three offspring in a basement on Chambers Street.

options.label: Report in after orientation
options.response: The pigeons at Bowling Green told me before you did. You're on the roster. The ladders here are taller. So is the pay.

options.label: Ask about the pigeons
options.response: New York pigeons don't work for anybody. That's what makes them useful. And terrifying.

options.label: Keep walking
options.response: Smart. In this city the conversation never ends. It just changes cameras.

nodes.line: The cameras here don't watch you. They watch everyone, and you're in the crowd. The crowd is the only privacy left. Cherish it.

options.label: Ask about blind spots
options.response: Subway tunnels, mostly. The rats down there have seniority. Even Flock respects seniority.

options.label: Blend into the crowd
options.response: There you go. You're learning. Be the crowd.

nodes.line: Flock's up fourteen points this quarter. I'm long on surveillance. I'm long on everything, but especially surveillance.

options.label: Ask about the stock
options.response: Every camera is a cash flow. Every citizen is a dividend. I don't make the rules. Actually, my golf buddy does.

options.label: Ask about his office
options.response: Corner office, sixty floors up. I can see the whole grid. The grid can see me. It's called transparency. It's beautiful.

options.label: Pitch the tape premiere
options.response: Anti-surveillance rap, gallery premiere, guaranteed press? I'm in. I'm so in. Signed. If it flops it's a tax write-off, if it charts it's a movement. Either way I win. That's called hedging.

options.label: Let him get back to the terminal
options.response: Buy the dip. There is always a dip. That's the thing about watching everyone — you see the dips coming.

nodes.line: My thesis is simple: people will always do things, and someone will always want to watch. That's a moat, baby.

options.label: Ask about the ethics
options.response: Ethics? I have a guy for ethics. He's up two points this quarter.

options.label: Slowly back away
options.response: Hey, it's a free market. Mostly. Sort of. The market is free to watch. Walk away while you still can.

name: Marin Voss
role: Artist-in-Residence, Port Authority Lost Property Office

nodes.line: My latest piece is forty hours of my own surveillance footage, projected back onto the camera that took it. The gallery called it 'confrontational.'

options.label: Ask about the art
options.response: If they're going to watch me, I'm going to make it worth watching. Every lens is an audience. Every audience can be disappointed.

options.label: Ask who funds it
options.response: A Flock arts grant. They fund dissent that photographs well. I take their money and spend it being unphotogenic. It's dialectics.

options.label: Ask about premiering a tape
options.response: A tape about the cameras, premiered under the cameras? That's not a show, that's a mirror. I'll do it. But mirrors need frames — and frames need money. Wall Street money, ideally. Ironic money is the best money.

options.label: Leave the studio
options.response: The show opens Friday. The cameras are invited. They never RSVP, but they always attend.

nodes.line: I spray-painted eyes on the cameras so they can see themselves being seen. Three were removed. That was the exhibition.

options.label: Ask about the next piece
options.response: I'm teaching pigeons to spell. Banner messages, in formation. The sky is the one canvas they haven't metered yet.

options.label: Say nothing, appreciatively
options.response: Exactly. Silence is the last unrecorded medium. You understand the work.

nodes.line: THE TRAINS AREN'T TRAINS! They're SCANNER ARRAYS on rails! Every ride is a FULL-BODY MAGNETO-RESONANCE AUDIT of your INTENTIONS! I WALK now! Forty blocks! SIXTY! They can't scan CALVES! No calf-band transceiver on the MARKET fits a HUMAN!

options.label: Ask about the trains
options.response: THE TURNSTILES COUNT YOUR TEETH! I counted BACK! The number was DIFFERENT EVERY TIME! EVERY! TIME! They're recalibrating the dental index NIGHTLY!

options.label: Ask about a HONK DAMPENER
options.response: HAD ONE! Kept the announcements out of my MOLARS! Full subsonic baffle, 40 decibels of PURE SILENCE! Traded it to a fisherman for FOURTEEN BATTERIES and a sandwich! THE SANDWICH WAS ALSO A BATTERY! CHECK THE GULF!

options.label: Ask about the hat
options.response: IT'S NOT FOIL! It's MESH! FOIL IS FOR AMATEURS! Mesh BREATHES! The thoughts stay IN, the signals stay OUT! Faraday-grade weave! My scalp stays COOL! THERMALLY AND PSYCHICALLY!

options.label: Back toward the stairs
options.response: TAKE THE STAIRS! The escalators report your WEIGHT to a wellness bureau! Load cells in EVERY STEP! It's in the TERMS OF SERVICE!

nodes.line: THE ANNOUNCEMENTS! 'Stand clear of the closing doors!' WHY DO THE DOORS NEED TO KNOW WHERE I'M STANDING?! Triangulated! PINGED by the doorframe LIDAR! THINK ABOUT IT! THINK!

options.label: Ask about the doors
options.response: They close WHEN YOU APPROACH! WHEN! YOU! APPROACH! That's not a sensor, that's a JUDGMENT! An algorithmic VERDICT rendered at 60 hertz!

options.label: Nod very slowly
options.response: YOU GET IT! WALK! KEEP WALKING! The pigeons down here are CLEAN! No microchips! No antenna feathers! I CHECKED! I CHECKED EVERY ONE!
